title: The Void
subtitle: KEYBOARD · MOVEMENT · TIME
description: Guide a small living flame across a tiled floor in empty space. Use W/A/S/D or the arrow keys.
explanation: FireHero is a component that stores the character's movement speed. Each frame, the control system checks which keys are held and builds a direction vector. We normalize the vector so diagonal movement is not faster. Then we multiply by speed and frame time (delta_secs) to get this frame's movement distance. The floor is a checkerboard of simple 3D tiles. The fire is three glowing cones whose scale and angle wobble slightly. Movement is bounded by the tile field; collision and gravity come later.
algorithm:
direction = normalize(keyboard input)
position += direction × speed × delta time
learning_goals: Translate held keyboard keys into a direction vector.
Explain why the direction is normalized before applying speed.
Trace how speed and frame time produce a movement distance.
review_points: What values can the direction vector have when no keys are held?
Why would diagonal movement be faster if the vector were not normalized?
What changes when movement is multiplied by delta_secs?
practice_tasks: Change FireHero speed and describe how far the fire moves in the same time.
Remove the normalization in a temporary experiment and compare diagonal movement.
Add a key that moves the fire more slowly, using a separate speed value.
